about.title: Santa Ana Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Ana logged 1,708 injury collisions in 2025, with 2,383 people hurt and 33 lives lost, according to public records. Much of that volume sits along 1st Street, Bristol Street, and both directions of I-5, and reported crashes cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when Orange County commuters are heading home. If one of those wrecks involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered: medical appointments, a car in the shop, an adjuster calling before you have even read the police report. LawProactive exists to take one task off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches Santa Ana residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file in most cases, but evidence from the scene fades far sooner. Reaching out early lets an attorney gather photos, witness contacts, and vehicle data while they still exist.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Ana Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines are shorter than they look
items.desc: California allows two years to file most car accident lawsuits, but a claim involving a city, county, or state vehicle or road can require notice within six months. An attorney can pin down which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame; your share is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. Insurers sometimes overstate that percentage, and an attorney pushes back with evidence.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in ordinary car accident cases. That means representation is within reach whether your injuries are modest or severe.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my I-5 crash in Santa Ana. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use your words to argue you were partly at fault, which lowers your recovery under comparative fault. Report the crash to your own insurer as your policy requires, but keep the details brief and factual.

items.question: What evidence should I hold onto after a Santa Ana car accident?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the roadway, and any visible injuries, along with the Santa Ana Police or CHP report number. Save medical records, repair estimates, and the names of anyone who saw the collision. If a nearby business on Bristol Street or 1st Street may have camera footage, note the location quickly, since recordings are often overwritten within days.

items.question: How does LawProactive work, and what does it cost me?
items.answer: LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. You share the basics of your crash, and we match you with an independent personal injury attorney who takes Orange County car accident cases. That attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
